checked_claims: AFI credits Susan Sarandon as Louise [Elizabeth Sawyer], Geena Davis as Thelma Dickinson, Harvey Keitel as Hal Slocumbe, and credits Ridley Scott and Callie Khouri in the stated roles.
AFI's synopsis and history support the Arkansas departure and ensuing journey framing; the article presents this as a film-reading prompt, not an unsupported factual scene claim.
The Academy's 1992 ledger records Davis and Sarandon as Actress in a Leading Role nominees, Jodie Foster as winner for The Silence of the Lambs, and Khouri as Original Screenplay winner.

The Academy film roster visibly groups five categories but lists six individual nominee entries because Davis and Sarandon share the actress category. The article's six-nomination wording is supportable as individual nominee entries; it should not be read as six distinct categories.
items.distractor_review: Davis played Thelma, Keitel played Hal, and Streep was only an earlier contender, not a final-cast Louise. Sarandon is the unique answer.
